statement: In people dependent on heroin going through supervised withdrawal, in three randomized trials from Australia, Germany and the USA (148 people, published 1985 to 2008, pooled in a Cochrane review searched to November 2015), clonidine or lofexidine compared with placebo reduced the chance of severe withdrawal, from about 59 to about 19 in 100 in the review's illustration (risk ratio 0.32, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.57), and more people completed the withdrawal treatment, about 56 against 29 in 100 (risk ratio 1.95, 1.34 to 2.84). Both results held when the one trial at high risk of bias was left out. The medicines brought more side effects: drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth and low blood pressure, and in the newest trial 4 of 35 people stopped lofexidine because of side effects against none of 33 on placebo. Two of the three trials were in hospital, and no included trial is described as involving fentanyl. Certainty: moderate. Status: replicated.
plain: In three trials, people coming off heroin or methadone who got clonidine or lofexidine had severe withdrawal less often than people who got a dummy pill, and more of them finished the withdrawal treatment. The medicines can make people sleepy or dizzy and lower blood pressure. The trials were small and old, and none was in people withdrawing from fentanyl.
population: People dependent on heroin in supervised withdrawal, inpatient or outpatient, in three randomized trials (Batey 1987, Benos 1985, Yu 2008) pooled in a Cochrane review
exposure: Clonidine or lofexidine as the main withdrawal medicine
outcome: Severe withdrawal during the withdrawal episode, with completion of withdrawal treatment and adverse effects reported alongside
magnitude: Severe withdrawal: RR 0.32 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.57), 3 trials, 148 participants, GRADE moderate; illustrative 589 per 1000 with placebo against 188 per 1000; without the high-risk trial RR 0.28 (0.09 to 0.83), 117 participants. Completion: RR 1.95 (1.34 to 2.84), 3 trials, 148 participants, moderate; 288 against 561 per 1000; without the high-risk trial RR 2.12 (1.40 to 3.19). Adverse effects not pooled: hypotension 18% against 0%, insomnia 42% against 9%, stopping for adverse effects 4 of 35 against 0 of 33 (Yu 2008); drowsiness and dizziness 7 of 16 against 0 of 15 (Batey 1987).

evidence.extracted: Severe withdrawal, alpha2 agonist (clonidine or lofexidine) against placebo: RR 0.32 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.57), 3 trials, 148 participants, GRADE moderate (downgraded for few events); illustrative 589 per 1000 with placebo against 188 per 1000. Leaving out the high-risk trial (Batey 1987): RR 0.28 (0.09 to 0.83), 117 participants.

evidence.locator: Summary of findings 2; Results › Effects of interventions › 1 › (d) Completion of treatment, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: Completion of withdrawal treatment, alpha2 agonist against placebo: RR 1.95 (1.34 to 2.84), 3 trials, 148 participants, GRADE moderate; illustrative 288 per 1000 with placebo against 561 per 1000. Without Batey 1987: RR 2.12 (1.40 to 3.19), 117 participants.

evidence.locator: Results › Effects of interventions › 1 › (c) Adverse effects, 1st to 3rd paragraphs
evidence.extracted: Sedation and dry mouth about twice as common with clonidine as with placebo (Benos 1985); drowsiness and dizziness in 7 of 16 on clonidine against 0 of 15 on placebo (Batey 1987); with lofexidine against placebo, blood pressure fell, hypotension 18% against 0% and insomnia 42% against 9%, and 4 of 35 against 0 of 33 stopped treatment for adverse effects (Yu 2008).

evidence.locator: Characteristics of included studies, Batey 1987, Benos 1985 and Yu 2008; Results › Description of studies › Participant characteristics, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: The pooled placebo trials are not named in the text; their group sizes (Batey 1987, 31, outpatient clinic, Australia; Benos 1985, 49, inpatient, Germany; Yu 2008, 68, inpatient, multiple US sites, terminated early for significant findings) add up to 148 (editors' arithmetic). Across the review, 19 of 26 trials involved withdrawal from heroin or other short-acting opioids; no trial is described as involving fentanyl.

risk_of_bias.note: One of the three trials was at high risk of reporting bias and sequence generation was unclear in another, but both results hold without the high-risk trial; the Cochrane review did not rate down for this.

inconsistency.note: All three trials point the same way.

indirectness.note: The claim is worded for supervised withdrawal from heroin or methadone in these trials and says that none involved fentanyl.

imprecision.note: 148 participants and few events, as the review rated.

publication_bias.note: Not investigated by the review (too few studies); not rated down, recorded as unknown.

grade.reasoning: Randomized trials start high (METHODS 6.3). Imprecision -1 gives moderate, matching the Cochrane review's own GRADE rating for both outcomes, which the card follows. Status replicated: three independent trials in three countries, all in the same direction. The adverse-effect findings are narrative and qualify the benefit; the claim does not rank clonidine against lofexidine.
